findings.title: `cancelAllTerminated` leaves `failed`/`terminated` state files intact; new state-based guard keeps blocking starts after bulk cleanup
findings.rationale: `cancelAllTerminated` removes only `.specrunner/local/<slug>/` (the machine-local sidecar dir) via `fs.rm(localSidecarDir(slug))`. It does NOT transition job states to `canceled` and does NOT touch state files at `specrunner/changes/<slug>/state.json`. Under the old pid-based guard, removing the sidecar was sufficient (dead pid allowed). Under the new state-based guard, `failed` and `terminated` are non-terminal occupants — their state files remain after bulk cleanup and continue to block new starts. A user who runs `job cancel --all-terminated` expecting to restart failed/terminated jobs will see 'Removed N job(s)' but subsequent starts are still rejected with SLUG_OCCUPIED pointing to the `failed`/`terminated` state. Only `job cancel <jobId>` (single-job cancel) properly transitions state to `canceled`. The design's Open Questions flagged a different risk for this function (sidecar collateral) but not this inverse problem.

findings.title: `ReopenCommand.prepare()` shows misleading 'Job not found' for terminal-only slugs after resolver change
findings.rationale: The new `resolveJobStateBySlug` returns only non-terminal jobs. For a slug whose only jobs are `canceled` or `archived` (both terminal), it returns `null`. `ReopenCommand.prepare()` falls through to `JobStateStore.resolveId`, which tries to match the slug string against UUID job-ID prefixes — fails with 'no job ID starts with my-slug' — and throws `JOB_NOT_FOUND`. The helpful status gate at line 139 ('Only awaiting-archive jobs are eligible for reopen') is now unreachable via the slug path for terminal-only slugs. `ResumeCommand.prepare()` was correctly updated with a terminal-job fallback check (resume.ts:107-121); `ReopenCommand.prepare()` received no equivalent update. The design D5 addressed only the new THROW case (ambiguous breach) but not the null-return case for terminal slugs.

observations.title: Function doc-comment for `cancelAllTerminated` says 'Bulk delete state files' but code only deletes sidecar directories
observations.rationale: The doc-comment says 'Bulk delete state files for all jobs in terminal status' but the implementation only calls `fs.rm(localSidecarDir(slug))`. No state files are touched. This pre-existing inaccuracy amplifies the confusion exposed by Finding 001.

observations.title: Inbox occupancy pre-check uses `JobStateStore.list` (silently skips corrupted states); guard uses `scanSlugOccupancy` (fails-closed)
observations.rationale: In the corrupted-state edge case, the inbox pre-check sees no non-terminal occupant and calls `runRunCore`; the guard detects corruption and throws SLUG_STATE_UNREADABLE which `runRunCore` swallows. The inbox would report 'started' incorrectly. Design D10 explicitly permits the `allJobStates`-filtered approach; the authoritative guard fires regardless. Impact is limited to the corrupted-state edge case.

observations.title: I-001: 定期 inbox tick で start action ごとに JobStateStore.list を再呼び出し
observations.rationale: buildEffects.startJob のデフォルト実装が JobStateStore.list(repoRoot) を start action ごとに呼んでいる。runInboxOrchestrator L88-91 で既に allJobStates をロード済みだが、buildEffects クロージャがその変数を参照できない構造のため再フェッチになっている。includeArchived: false なので archive 件数の増加でコストは伸びない。N_starts ≤ maxStartsPerRun（有限定数）かつ active state のみの走査で bounded されており、needs-fix の判定基準（単調増加する件数へ比例）には非該当。ただし定期経路に冗長なリスト呼び出しが生じている事実として記録する。

findings.title: scanSlugOccupancy swallows all errors from worktrees directory as 'no worktrees' — fail-open on non-ENOENT I/O failure
findings.rationale: The readdir(worktreesDir) catch-all at lines 88-110 silently suppresses all errors including EACCES, EIO, and other non-ENOENT failures. When .git/specrunner-worktrees/ exists but is unreadable, the guard treats the entire worktrees location as absent and allows a new start. This directly violates design.md D4: 'enumeration I/O fails (non-ENOENT)' must set unreadable and refuse. In contrast, tryReadStateJson at lines 139-143 correctly distinguishes ENOENT from other errors. Fix: check the error code in the catch block; only suppress ENOENT; set unreadable for all other codes.

findings.title: scanSlugOccupancy location 3 reads .specrunner/local/<slug>/state.json without marker.json gate — managed cancel leaves stale non-terminal state that permanently blocks new starts
findings.rationale: job-catalog.ts section 4 (unchanged) gates managed-runtime job enumeration on marker.json existence: if marker is absent the job is skipped. cancelSingleJob (normal cancel, no --purge) deletes marker.json when jobId matches but leaves .specrunner/local/<slug>/state.json intact with its pre-cancel status (running or awaiting-resume). scanSlugOccupancy location 3 reads state.json directly, bypassing the marker gate. Result: after normal cancel of a managed job, job ls shows nothing (catalog skips absent-marker job), but assertSlugUnoccupied returns nonTerminal.length=1 and throws SLUG_OCCUPIED. User cannot start a new job for the slug and cannot see the blocking job — stuck without manual file deletion or --purge. Only normal managed-runtime cancel (no --purge) triggers this; cancelAllTerminated and --purge both remove the entire directory. The stale-state residue must be eliminated either at write time (cancel updates state.json) or at read time (scan gates on marker).

options.label: Option A: scanSlugOccupancy location 3 gates on marker.json (read-side fix, mirrors job-catalog.ts section 4)
options.consequence: Scan skips location 3 when marker.json is absent, consistent with all other consumers. Low risk — scan is read-only. Does not clean up the stale state.json file; leaves a silent residue on disk that could confuse future tooling.

options.label: Option B: cancelSingleJob overwrites .specrunner/local/<slug>/state.json with the canceled state after deleting the marker (write-side fix)
options.consequence: State file reflects actual canceled status regardless of which consumer reads it. More thorough and consistent. Adds a new write path to cancelSingleJob; best-effort only to avoid blocking the cancel on a write failure.

observations.rationale: The code reviewer noted this in review-feedback-002.md I-001 with the observation that operational risk is low. From a cross-boundary perspective the D4 fail-closed contract is directly violated, hence classified as medium rather than informational.

observations.title: `repairSlugOccupancySidecar` ignores `scanResult.unreadable` — reports success when unreadable state co-exists with mismatch
observations.rationale: The function destructures only `{ nonTerminal }` from the scan result, discarding `unreadable`. If a slug has a corrupted state file (setting `unreadable`) alongside a valid non-terminal job (setting `nonTerminal.length === 1`) and a sidecar mismatch, the repair re-points the sidecar and returns a success message. However, `assertSlugUnoccupied` checks `result.unreadable !== null` before `nonTerminal.length >= 1`, so a subsequent `job start` still fails with `SLUG_STATE_UNREADABLE`. The repair message implies completion when an additional blocker remains. Requires the unusual three-way combination of: corrupted state file + valid non-terminal job + sidecar mismatch. The guard invariant (fail-closed) is intact.

observations.title: Doctor check does not inspect `result.unreadable` — gives false-clean for corrupted slugs that block starts
observations.rationale: `discoverSlugs` uses `JobStateStore.list` which silently skips corrupted per-entry states, so slugs whose only state entry is corrupted never appear in `slugList` and the doctor check is never invoked for them. Even if invoked via explicit slug injection, the check only evaluates `nonTerminal.length` and `sidecarJobId`, never `result.unreadable`. A slug blocked by `SLUG_STATE_UNREADABLE` would receive a 'pass' verdict from doctor. This is a design-scope gap (doctor is specified for breach and mismatch detection) rather than a broken pre-existing invariant. The guard remains correctly fail-closed.
